suggestions.what: Pass a function's arguments as JS arguments.
suggestions.now: A function bound to a name, whose parameter is a tuple pattern, has a direct form with the parts as its JS parameters; a call with the tuple written out goes to it with no array (trial/853-jit-loops-args 43828037c9). A function made where it is passed keeps one argument.
== is still $R.eq, but $R.eq is now three lines whose first compares with ===, small enough for the engine to inline (0e055e04c9: Go had been slower with records as objects until then).

A recursive function's calls of itself in tail position are a for (;;) loop, its variables declared per pass (50b70d5a40). Calls of another function in tail position, and mutual recursion, are still calls, as in ReScript and Melange.

suggestions.what: Unbox options, and make constructors flat.
suggestions.now: Some(t) is still {$c: "Some", $v: t}, and Take(a, b, k) still holds its arguments in an inner array.

suggestions.what: Lay out labeled tuples as objects only.
suggestions.now: A tuple whose every entry is labeled is a plain object (9ec865976d), and a field read is the property behind a check: 0.63 of the time on the games.
